page.notes: The text begins with a fragment ("pterea"), so it is marked cont="true". The reading "ut" for printed "vt" and "uti" for "vti" follow the u/v rule; "Ubi" follows the same rule. Long s has been read as s throughout, so "fanguis", "fententiae", "effe" appear as sanguis, sententiae, esse. The line "Quis dubitat" has no marginal notes. The dark strip on the right edge is the binding and the edge of the neighbouring page, so it is not transcribed. Italic passages are as seen on the scan; the italic boundaries are approximate where the type is faint.
